html:
A Germanic people of late antiquity, known from the 3rd to the 6th centuries. The map shows them in 200 and 300 in southern Scandinavia, where Roman writers placed their origins.

The Heruli turn up in many places. In 267 and 268 a band of them, with Goths, sailed from the Black Sea and raided Greece, sacking Athens. Others raided the coasts of Gaul and Spain. In the 5th century Heruli fought in Attila's armies and then in the Roman army in Italy, and some backed Odoacer when he deposed the last western emperor in 476.

Their best known kingdom lay north of the middle Danube, until the Lombards crushed it around 508. Survivors entered the service of Byzantium and fought for Justinian I. The historian Procopius wrote that some Heruli went back to Scandinavia and settled near the Geats. After the 6th century they vanish from the records.
